intro.author: Unknown. Jewish tradition variously credits Mordecai (compare 9:20) or the 'men of the Great Assembly'; the book itself does not say.
intro.written: Some time after the reign of Xerxes I (486–465 BC), probably in the Persian period, though some scholars date it later. The Greek version adds several passages, including prayers, now found in the Apocrypha as the Additions to Esther.
intro.audience: Jews scattered throughout the Persian empire, and later generations who keep the festival of Purim
intro.setting: The story takes place in Shushan (Susa), a Persian royal capital, during the reign of Ahasuerus, usually identified as Xerxes I. It falls between the temple's completion (Ezra 6) and Ezra's return (Ezra 7), among Jews who had stayed in the east.
intro.purpose: To tell how the Jews were saved from a plot to destroy them and to explain the origin of the festival of Purim.
intro.bigIdea: Though God's name never appears in the book, he quietly works through ordinary choices and timely 'coincidences' to protect his people.

outline.title: Deliverance and the feast of Purim
